description: AI engine — KnowledgeGraph source-code parser, ContextEngine (retrieves relevant context for a question), OpenAIProvider (calls gpt-4o), LocalAIProvider (stub), AIProvider interface, and the full AITab chat UI. Depends on FEAT-001 (types, AppLens singleton, storage) and FEAT-002 (AppLensProvider context, tab slot). Independent of FEAT-004 (Triveni Point integration).
steps: Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/AIProvider.ts — export interface AIProvider { chat(messages: AIMessage[], context: ContextChunk[]): Promise<string>; isConfigured(): boolean; }. Export AIProviderFactory function: createAIProvider(config: AppLensConfig): AIProvider — returns OpenAIProvider if aiProvider='openai' and apiKey is set, else LocalAIProvider.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/OpenAIProvider.ts — implements AIProvider. Constructor receives apiKey: string and model: string (default 'gpt-4o'). Uses the openai npm package: import OpenAI from 'openai'. chat() method: builds a system prompt from context chunks (each chunk converted to a text block with its type label), then calls openai.chat.completions.create({ model, messages: [{role:'system', content: systemPrompt}, ...messages mapped to OpenAI format], stream: false }). Returns the first choice's message content. isConfigured() returns true if apiKey is non-empty. Handle errors gracefully: catch and re-throw with a human-readable message. Export OpenAIProvider.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/LocalAIProvider.ts — stub that implements AIProvider. isConfigured() returns false. chat() throws new Error('No AI provider configured. Add aiApiKey to AppLens.initialize() to enable AI features.'). Export LocalAIProvider.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/KnowledgeGraph.ts — parses TypeScript/TSX source files from projectRoot to build an internal graph. Uses React Native's built-in file system capabilities (via global __DEV__ context only). Since React Native does not have Node fs, KnowledgeGraph uses a pre-built static snapshot approach: export interface GraphNode { name: string; type: 'screen'|'component'|'hook'|'service'|'store'|'api'; file: string; dependencies: string[]; }. export class KnowledgeGraph { private nodes: GraphNode[] = []; addNode(node: GraphNode): void; getNodes(): GraphNode[]; findByName(name: string): GraphNode|undefined; findDependencies(name: string): GraphNode[]; findDependents(name: string): GraphNode[]; toSummary(): string — returns a formatted text summary of all nodes and their relationships. The actual parsing (reading source files) cannot happen at runtime in RN — provide a static buildFromManifest(manifest: GraphNode[]): KnowledgeGraph factory that accepts pre-parsed data. Also provide a toJSON() / fromJSON() pair. } IMPORTANT NOTE: the CodeIndexer (step 5) is the bridge that pre-parses source files using a Node.js script run at dev time, not at RN runtime.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/CodeIndexer.ts — a Node.js-compatible script (NOT a RN module) that: reads all .ts/.tsx files under a given projectRoot directory recursively (using Node's fs/path), extracts: component names (function/const declarations that start with uppercase), hook names (functions starting with 'use'), service names (classes or files ending in .service.ts or .api.ts), import relationships (parse import statements to build dependency edges). Outputs a GraphNode[] JSON array. Export function indexProject(projectRoot: string): Promise<GraphNode[]>. This file is only run in Node.js (e.g., via a CLI script) and its output is passed to KnowledgeGraph.buildFromManifest(). Include a comment at the top: '// Run in Node.js only — not imported by RN bundle'.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/ai/ContextEngine.ts — takes a user question and retrieves the most relevant context chunks. Constructor receives AppLensStorage and KnowledgeGraph. getRelevantContext(question: string): ContextChunk[] method: (1) extract keywords from question (simple split + stopword removal), (2) from network logs: find requests whose URL contains any keyword — take top 5 by recency, format as 'METHOD URL STATUS DURATION\nResponse: <truncated body>', (3) from console logs: find entries whose message contains any keyword — take top 10 by recency, format as 'LEVEL timestamp: message', (4) from events: find events whose name or properties string contains any keyword — take top 5, (5) from KnowledgeGraph: call toSummary() and include as one chunk if question mentions 'component', 'hook', 'service', 'flow', 'architecture', or 'how'. Assign relevance scores. Return array of ContextChunk sorted by relevanceScore desc. Keep total context under ~8000 tokens by truncating individual chunks. Export class ContextEngine.

Replace the placeholder /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/tabs/AITab.tsx with the full chat UI implementation. AITab: (1) reads config from AppLens.getConfig(), (2) creates/manages AIConversation state (messages: AIMessage[]) in component state, (3) has a FlatList of chat bubbles — user messages right-aligned (dark green bg), assistant messages left-aligned (#1a1a1a bg, monospace-friendly), (4) at bottom: TextInput + Send button row, (5) on Send: append user message, call ContextEngine.getRelevantContext(question), call AIProvider.chat(messages, context), append assistant message, (6) show a loading indicator (ActivityIndicator) while waiting, (7) if AIProvider.isConfigured() returns false: show a setup prompt explaining how to configure the AI key, (8) show a system message on first load: 'AppLens AI is ready. I have access to your network logs, console output, events, and app structure. Ask me anything.' (9) each message shows timestamp. The AITab creates a ContextEngine and AIProvider instances using the AppLens singleton config. Export AITab.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAIProvider.chat() correctly calls the openai package and returns assistant text
LocalAIProvider.isConfigured() returns false and chat() throws a descriptive error
ContextEngine.getRelevantContext() returns network, log, and event chunks filtered by question keywords
KnowledgeGraph.toSummary() returns a readable text representation of all nodes and relationships
AITab shows chat bubbles, a text input, send button, and loading indicator
AITab gracefully shows configuration instructions when no AI API key is set
